title: Who walks away when a loved AI app goes bust (derived carousel, carries Mon 9 Nov follow.the.money, piece b358e788)

five_whys.q: Why is Disney hiring Character.AI's staff through a bankruptcy court?
five_whys.a: So it gets the team and the code while the lawsuits stay with what is left of Character.AI.

five_whys.q: Why does Disney want an AI team at all?
five_whys.a: Its $1 billion plan to put its characters in OpenAI's Sora app died when OpenAI shut Sora in March 2026.

five_whys.q: Why did that push Disney to buy rather than rent again?
five_whys.a: Renting meant its plans lived on someone else's app, and that app closed without warning.

five_whys.q: Why is this bigger than Disney?
five_whys.a: Netflix bought an AI film start-up for a reported $587 million and Warner Music bought Sureel AI: big firms are moving from renting AI to owning it.

five_whys.q: Why should an everyday business person care?
five_whys.a: Most businesses rent their AI; when its maker is bought or goes bust, the users are left with the empty box, so check the maker now and have a plan B.

cards.headline: Millions loved Character.AI. It went bust
cards.line: An app for chatting with made-up characters. It filed for bankruptcy on 12 October.
cards.picture: Cover scene: a chat app on a phone, alone on an auction block under a spotlight, a lot tag hanging off it

cards.headline: Google hired its founders first.
cards.line: In 2024 Google reportedly paid $2.7 billion to use its tech and hire its founders. The first warning sign.
cards.picture: A timeline: Aug 2024 the founders walk out to Google, Oct 2026 the app goes bust

cards.headline: Then Disney's AI video deal died.
cards.line: Disney's $1 billion deal put its characters in OpenAI's Sora app. OpenAI shut Sora in March.
cards.picture: Disney's characters locked outside a shuttered Sora shopfront

cards.headline: So Disney is hiring Character.AI's team.
cards.line: Jobs for 66 staff through the bankruptcy court. The lawsuits stay behind with the shell.
cards.picture: 66 small figures walking across to Disney, a pile of lawsuits left on the empty floor

cards.headline: Big firms now own their AI instead of renting.
cards.line: Renting is using another firm's AI. Netflix bought an AI film start-up for a reported $587 million.
cards.picture: Three buyers, each with a SOLD tag: Disney, Netflix, Warner Music, an arrow from RENT to OWN
cards.source: The Hollywood Reporter on Netflix and InterPositive (2026); also Warner Music Group buying Sureel AI, PR Newswire (June 2026)

cards.headline: Your AI could vanish too.
cards.line: If its maker is bought or goes bust, users are left with the empty box.
cards.picture: An open, empty box with a chat bubble fading out of it

cards.headline: Check who makes your AI.
cards.line: Founders still there? Your tool its main product? Short of cash? Collecting lawsuits?
cards.picture: A four-line checklist, one box per question

cards.headline: Pick your plan B now.
cards.line: If two answers worry you, try another tool on one real task this month. Follow for more.
cards.picture: A spare key on a hook, Follow for more over the centred wordmark

read_back.reader: Fresh reader A (Haiku, a small-business owner, headlines only, once; round 2)

answers.what: An AI company collapsed, and businesses renting AI could lose access to it too.
answers.happened: Character.AI, loved by millions, went bust, and Google hired its founders first.
answers.why: Its founders went to Google first and its big partner's plans changed, so it was left weak.
answers.so_what: If an AI tool I rely on can vanish overnight, my business could lose a key service with no warning.
answers.do: Check who makes each AI tool I use and pick a backup option now.

read_back.reader: Fresh reader B (Sonnet, a 15-year-old, headlines only, once; round 2)

answers.what: A popular AI chatbot app called Character.AI ran out of money and collapsed even though millions used it.
answers.happened: Google hired the founders first, then OpenAI shut the app Disney relied on, so Disney is hiring the Character.AI team.
answers.why: Big companies are now building and owning their own AI instead of paying to use someone else's.
answers.so_what: The AI apps I use could disappear suddenly if the company behind them goes under.
answers.do: Find out which company makes the AI I use and have a backup option ready.
